text:
Jamie Benn got his 1,000th NHL point this week, a captain's milestone in a city where he has spent his whole career. It landed in a week when the louder conversation was about Jason Robertson: insiders floating blockbuster trade ideas and analysts doubting he signs long term in Dallas. Neither story has changed how the Stars play, which is well.

Dallas is 11-6-2 with 24 points and has taken 52% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances). The interesting part is that it has scored about seven fewer goals than its chances usually produce and allowed about seven fewer, so the goaltending has covered for a quiet offense. Jake Oettinger shut out Buffalo twice. Our playoff odds sit at 81%.

The blue line is thinner than usual. Miro Heiskanen has missed games and was listed as doubtful, and Lian Bichsel is out at least two weeks. Thomas Harley and Nils Lundkvist have been the best pair, with 59% of the chances and an 11-7 goal edge.

Up front, Mikko Rantanen is on a goal streak, and his line with Wyatt Johnston and Sam Steel has dominated the chances even if the goals haven't followed. What we'd watch: whether the Robertson line with Roope Hintz and Tyler Seguin finds its game, and how the Stars handle the noise if the rumors keep coming.
